summary: Archetype-to-visual-need map produced for all ~103 content pages across 8 archetypes. 70% of pages are hero-only (no body visuals). Only 8% have genuinely rich body-visual coverage (2+ unique illustrations or inline image series). Highest-need archetypes: diagnostic troubleshooters (missing decision trees), fee-definers (missing annotated bill sections), and comparison pages (missing matrix graphics).
findings: ARCHETYPE TAXONOMY: 8 archetypes identified — Diagnostic Troubleshooter (19 pages), Fee-Definer (23), How-To Action (32), Product Page (7), Hub (4), Tool-Calculator (2), Bill-Anatomy Explainer (5), Comparison (11). Overlap exists (e.g., bill-anatomy explainers overlap fee-definers).

VISUAL COVERAGE RATES: 79 of 113 article image directories have ONLY a hero image (70%). 36 of 113 have at least one body visual (32%). Only 9 of 113 have 2+ meaningful body visuals or inline image series (8%).

BEST-VISUALIZED PAGES: how-sewer-charges-work-on-your-water-bill (6 files: 3 body + 3 hero variants), 28-utility-reconnection-fee-explained (3 body + hero + inline), 21-past-due-balance (2 body: bill-anatomy + timeline), moving-utilities-checklist (3 checklist icons), can-utility-shut-off-service (3 crisis sequence imgs), what-is-ccf-on-a-water-bill (2 body: convert diagram + normal usage chart).

INLINE-IMAGE SERIES: 3 pages use Magica batch-generated inline series — why-electric-bill-changes-month-to-month (4 subsets: TOU/tier diagram, demand/peak chart, delivery/supply split, billing calendar), why-did-my-utility-bill-go-up-this-month (4: 3-buckets diagram, billing-days chart, estimated-correction, self-check photo), how-utility-rates-fees-usage-work-together (4: layered model, rate-shapes, fixed-vs-variable, ripple illustration). These are the gold standard for body visuals on the site.

DIAGNOSTIC TROUBLESHOOTER GAP: 19 pages, 0 have decision-tree graphics despite 'check A → if yes then B → if no then C' being the core content pattern. Only water-meter-running-when-no-water-used has a decision tree. Every other troubleshooter is text-only. Evidence: content/blog/03-why-is-my-electric-bill-so-high.md (hero+V2+inline only; no body images at all).

FEE-DEFINER GAP: 23 pages. Only 3 have body visuals beyond hero+inline (fee breakdown chart in taxes-fees-breakdown.webp, past-due bill anatomy, reconnection fee breakdown). Zero pages show the fee highlighted/annotated on a real bill section — the most natural visual type for this archetype. Evidence: content/blog/17-what-is-customer-charge-on-utility-bill.md (hero only).

HOW-TO ACTION STRONG POINTS: 32 pages, ~25% have body visuals. Best examples: how-to-read-a-water-meter (dial-meter-reading.webp with labeled annotation), what-is-ccf-on-a-water-bill (ccf-convert chain, ccf-normal band chart), how-sewer-charges (3 diagrams). Water-meter reading guides have consistently better illustration than electric/gas meter guides. Evidence: how-to-read-electric-meter.md and how-to-read-gas-meter.md have hero only — contrast with water meter page which has labeled dial diagram.

BILL-ANATOMY EXPLAINERS: Strongest visual coverage at ~60% with body visuals. electric-bill-breakdown-understanding-line-items has ebill-4numbers.webp (annotated bill) and ebill-tou.webp (TOU diagram). utility-bills-costs-explained and hub pages (electricity-explained, gas-explained, water-explained) all share bill-anatomy.webp — a reusable annotated bill illustration.

PRODUCT PAGE COVERAGE: 7 pages, ~35% have body visuals, but none have comparison matrix graphics. gas-vs-electric-heating-cost-comparison and heat-pump-vs-gas-furnace-savings are text-only with hero, no side-by-side comparison visual. Evidence: grep shows no 'matrix' or 'comparison' in any page body image.

COMPARISON PAGE GAP: 11 pages, ~18% have body visuals. afue-vs-seer-vs-hspf-vs-cop, ductless-mini-split-vs-central-air, fixed-vs-variable-rate-electricity-plan are all hero-only. The most comparison-intensive pages have zero comparison graphics. Evidence: content/blog/afue-vs-seer-vs-hspf-vs-cop.md image: only hero.

CUSTOM_INLINE.WEBP: Appears in ~45 article directories as a single 1024×576px generic WebP. This is a sitewide placeholder sentinel — not article-specific content. It inflates the 'has body visual' count but provides near-zero engagement value. Distinct from the inline/ batch series (which are genuine article-specific illustrations).

IMAGE-SERP OPPORTUNITY: High potential for definitional pages (what-is-ccf-on-a-water-bill, what-is-a-kilowatt-hour, mcf-vs-ccf-vs-therms, what-is-customer-charge) and how-to meter-reading pages (how-to-read-a-water-meter, how-to-read-electric-meter, how-to-read-gas-meter) — these query types frequently trigger Google image packs. Low/no potential: crisis pages (can-utility-shut-off-service, past-due, reconnection fees) and highly specific fee pages (fuel-adjustment-charge, drought-surcharge). Medium: comparison pages (gas-vs-electric, heat-pump-vs-furnace, fixed-vs-variable) — image packs occasionally appear for these.
TOPIC-ICONS.SVG exists (static/images/topic-icons.svg) but is only used on hub/category pages. It is not leveraged for individual article body use — an immediate quick-win opportunity.

BILL-ANATOMY.WEBP is shared across 4 hub pages (electricity-explained, gas-explained, water-explained, utility-bills-costs). This reusable annotated-realia approach is the pattern to extend to individual fee pages.

ANNOTATION-SPRITE.SVG exists (static/images/annotation-sprite.svg) — a shared component for labeling bill sections/meter parts. Used by the water-meter reading pages but not electroly/gas meter pages. Unused potential for all fee-definer pages.
